title: Masked client_secret can be saved back as the real Wallabag secret
reasoning: GET /wallabag returns PASSWORD_MASK for an existing client_secret, but the update path only treats that sentinel specially for password. If a settings client loads the GET response and submits an unchanged form containing the masked client_secret, the PUT handler writes the mask into config.client_secret, destroying the real OAuth secret and breaking the integration.
reproduction: Configure Wallabag with a non-empty client_secret, call GET /wallabag, then submit the returned client_secret value unchanged to PUT /wallabag. The persisted client_secret becomes the mask string instead of the original secret.
recommendation: Handle client_secret the same way password is handled: skip updating it when the submitted value equals PASSWORD_MASK, and only clear/update it for explicit empty or real values.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise GET /wallabag masking or a GET-then-PUT unchanged-secret round trip; the existing matches found are unrelated digest/EPUB tests and cover-secret tests.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an API test that creates a WallabagConfig with client_secret and password, verifies GET /wallabag masks both fields, then PUTs the returned payload unchanged and asserts the stored client_secret and password remain the original values.
minimumFixScope: Change update_wallabag_config handling for client_secret in app/api/config.py and add a focused route-level regression test.
